claim: A Direct Connect gateway acts as a distributed set of BGP route reflectors outside the data traffic path, so it creates no single point of failure and no dependency on specific Regions. High availability is built in, so you do not need multiple gateways for it.

v: a distributed set of BGP route reflectors
it avoids creating a single point of failure
ev: docs/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-gateways-intro

A Direct Connect gateway is a virtual component of Direct Connect designed to act as a distributed set of BGP route reflectors. Because it operates outside the data traffic path, it avoids creating a single point of failure or introducing dependencies on specific AWS Regions. High availability is inherently built into its design, eliminating the need for multiple Direct Connect gateways.

claim: A Direct Connect gateway does not let gateway associations on the same gateway send traffic to each other. The exception is when a supernet is advertised across two or more VPCs whose virtual private gateways are associated to the same Direct Connect gateway and virtual interface.

scope: associations on one Direct Connect gateway
cond: exception: supernet advertised on the same virtual interface
ev: docs/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-gateways-intro

A Direct Connect gateway does not allow gateway associations that are on the same Direct Connect gateway to send traffic to each other (for example, a virtual private gateway to another virtual private gateway). An exception to this rule, implemented in November 2021, is when a supernet is advertised across two or more VPCs, which have their attached virtual private gateways (VGWs) associated to the same Direct Connect gateway and on the same virtual interface.

claim: A Direct Connect gateway will not route traffic between a VPN and a Direct Connect virtual interface. For that you create a VPN in the Region of the virtual interface and attach both to the same virtual private gateway.

No, an AWS Direct Connect gateway will not route traffic between a VPN and an AWS Direct Connect VIF. To enable this use case, you must create a VPN in the AWS Region of the VIF and attach the VIF and the VPN to the same VGW.

claim: A LAG has an attribute for the minimum number of connections that must be operational. By default new LAGs set it to 0. If you set a higher value, the whole LAG becomes non-operational when fewer connections than that are operational.

ev: docs/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/lags

All LAGs have an attribute that determines the minimum number of connections in the LAG that must be operational for the LAG itself to be operational. By default, new LAGs have this attribute set to 0. You can update your LAG to specify a different value—doing so means that your entire LAG becomes non-operational if the number of operational connections falls below this threshold.

claim: A LAG does not make connectivity to AWS more resilient. It can protect against a single link failure, but not against a single device failure or device maintenance at AWS where the LAG terminates. AWS recommends connections at multiple Direct Connect locations.

it will not protect against a single device failure or device maintenance at AWS where your LAG is terminating
ev: www/directconnect/faqs

No, a LAG doesn't make your connectivity to AWS more resilient. If you have more than one link in your LAG, and if your minimum links are set to one, your LAG will let you protect against single link failure. However, it will not protect against a single device failure or device maintenance at AWS where your LAG is terminating.

This model provides resiliency against connectivity failures caused by a fiber cut or a device failure. It also helps prevent a complete location failure.

claim: Direct Connect supports resilience testing with AWS Fault Injection Service, which lets you test how applications respond when the BGP sessions over your virtual interfaces are disrupted.
q: How can you test Direct Connect BGP failover with AWS Fault Injection Service?
v: resilience testing with AWS Fault Injection Service
test and observe how your applications respond when Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) sessions over your Virtual Interfaces are disrupted
scope: AWS Fault Injection Service action for Direct Connect
ev: www/about-aws/whats-new/2025/12/direct-connect-resilience-testing-fault-injection-service

AWS Direct Connect now supports resilience testing with AWS Fault Injection Service (FIS), a fully managed service for running controlled fault injection experiments to improve application performance, observability, and resiliency. With this capability, you can test and observe how your applications respond when Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) sessions over your Virtual Interfaces are disrupted and validate your resilience mechanisms.
